The unresolved question: Is the model failing to learn the semantics, failing to reconstruct the evidence state, or failing while expressing the result? The experiment bundled these responsibilities together.
02

The conceptual change

The ontology is
the semantic model.

The trainer defines what the system means. Typed nodes and relationships represent that meaning. Semantic Ontology Morphology describes how their state and support change over time.

ONTOLOGY

What exists, and relates

Concept instances, assets, evidence and typed relationships.

MORPHOLOGY

What changes

New support, shared origins, withdrawal, contradiction and changing scope.

INTERPRETATION

What the change means

Whether concern should rise, persist, fall or remain uncertain.

Illustrative target behavior · not a model output
A Access origin AC Source correctionD Independent origin DH Threat hypothesis

Withdrawn does not mean forgotten.

The correction retires both reports of origin A. The history remains, but its current support is removed.

Retained access reports: 2
Active access origins: 0
Illustrative assessment: contextual

Node A grows with retained report volume; its withdrawn state changes the support edge. Volume is not confidence. Two reports of one origin are not independent corroboration. This explanatory semantic graph is not a diagram of literal neural connections.

Historical presence ≠ current support.
03

The failure we must preserve

It could name the correction
and still reason past it.

Some outputs acknowledged that evidence was retired, then used that same evidence—or credential activity—as current compromise support. Others cited graph nodes where report identities were required.

Semantic inconsistency

Evidence is withdrawn.
The warning still relies on it.

A completed response can be wrong. Valid syntax and a plausible explanation do not establish correct meaning.

Repetitive generation

The explanation repeats.
The answer never completes.

A loop can begin with the expected label. Repetition and retraction errors require separate tests.

The token cap stops the loop; it does not explain the wrong interpretation. Reference answers fit below 857 output tokens. The fixed comparison allowance was 1,536.

Read the measurement limits

All cases are same-author synthetic development controls. Known cases informed subsequent curriculum work. Fresh cases were frozen before training, but share the author, semantic motifs and reference policy. The previous adapter was not evaluated on the new fresh six. These are reference-agreement counts, not independent field accuracy or calibrated probabilities of attack.

Repetition flags narrative text of at least 36 words when a 12-word window occurs at least three times and duplicate-window fraction is at least 0.25. Graph-field repetition is excluded. Exact outputs and failed cases were retained without repair or admission back into training.

Current conclusion: the curriculum can change behavior, but the resulting model is not a reliable operational warning system.
05

Diagnosis before another guess

Five hypotheses.
No isolated root cause yet.

Numerical stability, matched prompts and recognized end tokens are verified. Reliable semantic interpretation is not. We need discriminating tests before treating any hypothesis as a fix.

1

Learning shortcuts

Tiny, related curricula may teach templates instead of conditional meaning. Test trained cases against equivalent cases with changed identifiers and ordering.

2

Reconstruction burden

The model may struggle to derive the current state from history. Supply explicit active/retracted facts while holding weights fixed.

3

Misaligned supervision

Long graph and prose targets may dominate the semantic decisions. Measure errors by output component before a separate supervision ablation.

4

Unverified training fit

Completed updates do not prove the model learned its own examples. Replay exact training cases first.

5

Generation feedback

An early mistake may create a repeating continuation. Compare continuation from mistaken and corrected prefixes.

These tests are planned. The completed interface audit matched sixty saved training and fifty-two validation records across v3/v4/v5, with no detected prompt-rendering or logged-length mismatch. That does not rule out every implementation or learning issue.

06

The target architecture

Train with large capacity.
Deliver a small footprint.

Training and deployment have different resource constraints. The teacher can be large and trained centrally. A refugee receives a finished local inference model.

Application responsibility

Maintain semantic facts

Identity, timing, provenance, active/retracted support and incident history.

→
Target AI capability

Interpret the change

Meaning, criticality, uncertainty and supporting evidence.

→
Reference tooling exists

Preserve warning continuity

Expose retained warning state before inference; surface incomplete results.

The facts-to-meaning boundary is an intended design, not a proven root-cause fix. Larger-teacher competence and successful student distillation remain unproven here. Warning-continuity tests use a simulated backend; real model-provider, phone and notification-delivery integration remain pending.

Broad window at second 10

01020304050607080910

Advance one second

02030405060708091011

Add the newest second. Expire the oldest. Keep nine overlapping seconds without recounting them as fresh evidence. A one-second window cadence is not a claim of one-second model inference.

Monitor broadly

Continue across intercepts until a meaningful change warrants attention.

Focus when warranted

Prioritize related entities and sequences while broad collection continues.

Retain the incident

Window expiry does not erase triggering evidence or imply clearance.

Resolve explicitly

Accept justified revision using current evidence and an explicit resolution policy.

Humanitarian target: recognize a threatening sequence early enough to support protective action. A Wi-Fi disruption followed by drone signatures is an illustrative reason for focused precautionary assessment, not proof by co-occurrence of causation or imminent assault.
07

Why the direction still matters

A testable path forward.

The promise is a model that understands evolving relationships well enough to revise its judgment. Tonight's experiments demonstrate pieces of learning—and expose the gap to reliability.

Make meaning explicit.
Teach how it changes.
Measure what survives.

Explicit semantics

An ontology gives trainers a defined model of the system, rather than an informal label collection.

Temporal interpretation

Morphology makes new support, contradiction and withdrawal central to the learning task.

Separate resource budgets

Teacher–student distillation offers a route from large training capacity to smaller deployment models; retention must be demonstrated.

NOWDiagnose failures
NEXT GATEProve teacher skill
TRANSFERDistill and verify
DEVICETest phone behavior
RELEASEReview field failures centrally
A warning must not wait for an essay. Output budgets must be explicit and configurable. Incomplete generation must preserve validated warnings and evidence, never silently mean “all clear.” More tokens alone cannot repair an incorrect interpretation.
